captions.linkedin:
There's a single number on every stock chart that predicts next-month returns better than 12 months of price history. 📊

It's the 52-week high.

George & Hwang (Journal of Finance, 2004) found that nearness to the 52-week high (current price divided by the trailing 52-week peak) dominates Jegadeesh-Titman individual-stock and industry momentum. In a horse race, the 52-week high signal wins.

Here's the complete logic:

🔹 RATIO. For each stock, compute (current price) / (52-week high). A number between 0 and 1.
🔹 RANK every stock by the ratio.
🔹 LONG the top 30% (stocks closest to their 52-week high).
🔹 SHORT the bottom 30% (stocks farthest below).
🔹 EQUAL-WEIGHTED, overlapping 6-month holds.
🔹 Forecasted returns do NOT reverse over subsequent years. This is persistent drift, not short-term mean reversion.

Why it works: anchoring bias. Investors treat the 52-week high as a psychological reference point. Stocks near the high face resistance from sellers using the anchor as an exit price. When they punch through, the anchor releases and the stock drifts higher with low turnover.

International studies confirmed the effect in 18 of 20 markets.
